findings.title: Past-due cleanup drops cancelled reminders before they are cancelled at SendGrid
findings.body: The handler deletes every email reminder whose scheduledDate is in the past before querying and cancelling `cancelled` reminders. If a booking is cancelled shortly before its reminder and the next 15-minute cron invocation occurs after the reminder's send time, this deletion removes the only cancellation record and no SendGrid cancellation request is made. The already scheduled SendGrid email can therefore still be delivered, which is precisely the case this change is intended to prevent. Cancelled reminders must be handled before cleanup, and cancellation should not depend on a cron execution occurring before `sendAt`.

findings.title: Standard reschedules still immediately consume SendGrid cancellation slots
findings.body: The reschedule flow passes `true` for `immediateDelete`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to call SendGrid immediately rather than mark the reminder as cancelled for the cron-based cleanup. This preserves the old behavior that accumulates SendGrid scheduled-send cancellations and hits the provider's 100 pending-cancellation limit during reschedules. Errors are swallowed by the helper and no `cancelled` flag is set as a fallback, so reminders whose immediate cancellation is rejected will still be sent.

findings.title: The cron's SendGrid client is never authenticated
findings.body: This module configures only `sgMail` with `sgMail.setApiKey`; it never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` for the separately imported `@sendgrid/client` instance. The new cancellation request at this line uses that client directly, so it will be sent without SendGrid authorization and fail. The catch only logs the failure, leaving the reminder in the database and allowing the email to be sent.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation writes are not awaited before completing booking cancellation
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but the nested `forEach` discards their promises. Consequently the booking cancellation request can complete while the email reminder's `cancelled` update or SMS cancellation/delete is still pending. In a serverless/request-scoped runtime those operations can be interrupted after the response, and the cron can observe the reminder before it is marked, resulting in a reminder being sent for a cancelled booking. Collect and await these operations (and apply the same treatment in the other modified cancellation paths).
